justification: Test the supplied reference as one source/label/identity module. E_graph supplies online joint endpoint forecasts, whereas E_credit attaches common-rescore predicted pIC50 of decoded terminal molecules to observed ancestors at state_time; label_clock=1.0 denotes terminal structure time. These are observed continued-Steer outcomes. Extinction remains censored. E_library supplies exact terminal-path identities: 28 paths, 23 unique terminal graphs, 14-26 teachers per learning time, and scores 7.733001-8.704806. Its minimum is below the elite threshold, so the target definition does not assert an elite-only library. The candidate reference identity is supplied by E_library and the execution contract; external artifact hashes were not independently verified here. The coordinate observable remains the incumbent endpoint_pointcloud on predicted_endpoint_world_A. Differentiate that reward through the unchanged flowr_endpoint_vjp endpoint map to generation coordinates; a temporal feature derivative supplies no spatial direction. Every formula, dose, parameter, and constraint originates from incumbent_program and is retained, including predictive_flow dosing, native_rms_ratio=0.33, teacher_neighbors=4, teacher_endpoint_temperature_A2=4.0, and teacher_score_beta=2.0. Teacher learning support is t=0 through 0.49; t=0.50 is a selection/current-state boundary and supplies no extra learning slice. E_control motivates a tail-focused screen: round04 gradient and unguided each yielded zero valid elites among 100 outputs, despite modest mean-score differences and separate strain differences. Neither those results nor retrospective terminal association establish prospective benefit. This decision permits the frozen paired screen, not deployment or a receptor-hotspot claim.
validation_hypotheses: Primary hypothesis: on the paired batch30 panel with master_seed=42 and n=50 per arm, this source replacement increases valid terminal elite count divided by all generated outputs versus the unchanged incumbent. Use the same terminal decoding/common-rescore protocol and fixed threshold_pic50=8.258901977539063. Report both counts, their difference, and uncertainty appropriate to the paired generated-output units; repeated trajectory times and donor clones are not independent replicates.

Useful-path hypothesis: an elite-yield gain is accompanied by increased unique elite terminal graphs. Report validity, all-output and valid-output final score distributions, and unique elite graphs together. A gain explained entirely by duplicate graphs or a validity-denominator change fails this useful-path hypothesis; strain improvement cannot substitute for affinity-tail improvement.

Secondary geometry hypothesis: fixed-source replacement does not materially worsen final strain. Report strain convergence counts and median/p90 strain per heavy atom separately from predicted affinity, without altering the reward, dose, or graph-transition policy to obtain this result.

Execution hypothesis: the candidate reference is usable by the same endpoint_pointcloud formula and flowr_endpoint_vjp path within the incumbent window and bounded guidance. Audit that only reference_sha256 and target_definition differ, that teacher queries use supplied learning support t=0 through 0.49, and that the t=0.50 boundary is not treated as a learned teacher slice.

A nonpositive candidate-control elite-yield difference fails this frozen screen. Zero elites in both arms or wide uncertainty is inconclusive for a small population effect. A reproducible difference at or below zero with uncertainty excluding a positive effect would falsify the proposed elite-yield benefit; a positive point estimate on this adaptively selected n=50 panel alone does not establish a population benefit.
failure_modes: Endpoint pointcloud similarity can increase without improving decoded terminal predicted affinity; teacher labels do not identify receptor regions, spatial hotspots, or interaction energies. No affinity-head gradient or new spatial target is justified.

Observed Steer futures, survival censoring, per-ancestor maxima, donor preselection, and shared ancestry can bias teacher credit. The 669 valid terminal records contain only 20 unique elite graphs among 34 elite records; neither clone counts nor repeated times establish native continuation utility or causal benefit.

Sparse and changing early observability (17/700 at t=0, 37/700 at t=0.25) can weaken early transfer. Late coverage and the t=0.50 boundary do not justify an early-to-late affinity trend, extrapolated teacher support, or additional controller changes.

The library contains subthreshold labels and only 23 unique terminal graphs. Its fixed weighting may dilute the tail signal or concentrate duplicate paths; transfer from preselected donor batches 0-13 to batch30 can fail, and no supplied batch-specific direction agreement resolves that risk.

A single adapted screening batch has limited power for rare elites. Score gains, validity loss, or strain changes must remain distinct outcomes; predicted pIC50 is not measured affinity, and a changed chemical graph alone supplies no demonstrated mechanism for quality loss.
